title: Branching Probe Controller: Kernel Affinity, Probe Heuristics, and Graceful Rollback Playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Implement a 'Branching Probe Controller' in the inference runtime that issues micro-probes (short prefill/partial-decode requests) to candidate model variants, scores kernel affinity and acceptance likelihood, and executes a deterministic graceful rollback when optimistic branches fail acceptance checks. Scope covers the routing policy, probe orchestration, acceptance metrics surface, rollback choreography, and observability plumbing--not model training or model repository changes.

Motivation: We want lower-latency fast-path responses by speculatively decoding on cheaper/faster kernels or model variants while maintaining quality and reliability guarantees. Existing optimistic routers re-use coarse heuristics (latency buckets, static model priority). This controller adds per-request probe signals plus kernel affinity scoring to make better acceptance decisions and a standardized rollback playbook when probes mispredict.

Non-goals: full A/B rollout UI, autoscaling changes, or new quantization formats. This ticket focuses on runtime orchestration and telemetry surfaces required for SLO-safe speculative decoding.
design_decisions: Micro-probes are limited to <32 tokens and must execute with bypassed KV cache to avoid large cache pollution.
Probe routing performs parallel dispatch to up to 2 candidate kernels/model variants chosen by kernel-affinity score and cost tier.
Acceptance metric uses a composite score: normalized logits delta + token-by-token agreement heuristic + decoding runtime confidence. Thresholds are configurable per route.

If probe acceptance fails, controller triggers deterministic rollback: cancel outstanding speculative decode, replay request to fallback model variant with preserved user-visible continuity (stream retraction token).

Controller computes kernel-affinity fingerprints from model architecture metadata + recent decode telemetry, favoring kernels with historically lower per-token p95 latency for similar sequence lengths.
No schema change to public API; we add internal flags and headers for canary rollout and debugging only.
Telemetry and tracing are first-class: every probe and acceptance decision emits events with request_id, probe_id, kernel_fingerprint, latency_ms, acceptance_score, and decision_reason.
Fallback path must be cold-start safe: guardrails prevent infinite rollback loops by counting probe attempts per request.
Configuration follows per-route JSON policy stored in config-service and hot-reloaded; default is conservative (only probe for P1 routes during canary).
telemetry_events: spec_probe.created - emitted when a micro-probe dispatched (fields: request_id, probe_id, candidates)
spec_probe.result - probe result (probe_id, kernel_fingerprint, latency_ms, topk_logits_snapshot)
spec_probe.acceptance - acceptance_score and accepted boolean (with thresholds used)
spec_decode.rollback - emitted when rollback is triggered (request_id, probe_id, reason)
spec_decode.path - final path used for full decode (speculative|fallback|fallback-after-rollback)
kernel_affinity.update - periodic aggregation of kernel scores per model family and seqlen bucket
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Unit/integration tests and simulator: implement controller behind feature flag and validate deterministic rollback in local sim.
Phase 1 - Internal canary: enable for <1% of production routes (non-critical P3) and validate telemetry for 72 hours.
Phase 2 - Expanded canary: increase to 5% with automated SLO guardrails (latency p95 and error rate), monitor cost delta.
Phase 3 - Route opt-in: surface controls to Route Owners (via console) to enable speculative probes per route with guidance.
Abort criteria: >2x error rate increase, >15% p95 latency regression on route, or acceptance false-negative rate >10% leading to visible truncation artifacts.

risks_mitigations: Risk: Probe adds extra work and increases cost. Mitigation: conservative default caps on probe frequency and token budget per request; billing tags for probe work for cost visibility.
Risk: Probe false acceptances degrade quality. Mitigation: composite acceptance score + gradual threshold tuning via simulator + rollback playback tests.

Risk: Rollback race can stream duplicate tokens. Mitigation: streaming protocol supports retraction tokens and client-visible marker for rollback path; test coverage ensures no duplicate-commit states.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample probes for full payload snapshots; aggregate metrics for daily trends.
Risk: Kernel affinity cache staleness after infra changes. Mitigation: TTL-based cache and active refresh on failed acceptance rates per kernel fingerprint.
